content.title: Common Code Questions
content.summary: Residents are encouraged to resolve neighborhood issues amicably before contacting Code Enforcement. Property owners are responsible for snow removal from sidewalks within 24 hours, maintaining yards free of weeds and rubbish, and ensuring vehicles are operable and parked appropriately. Additionally, regulations exist regarding signage, fencing permits, and the maintenance of trees and shrubs to prevent obstruction of sidewalks and city signs.
content.body:
Before reporting neighborhood concerns to Code Enforcement, please consider trying to resolve the issues productively between neighbors. Learn about[Resolving Neighborhood Conflicts](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1003/Neighborhood-Conflict-Resolution).

## Snow Removal

All[ice, slush, and snow must be removed from sidewalks](https://www.arvadaco.gov/411/Municipal-Code-for-Shoveling-Walkways) adjoining the property within 24 hours after the snow stops falling. It is the owner/occupant's responsibility to maintain the property out to the traveled portion of the roadway (including sidewalks, curbs, and gutters).

## Barking Dogs/Pets and Wildlife

Arvada Animal Management is a unit of the Arvada Police Department. Animal Management [enforces all City ordinances related to animals](https://www.arvadaco.gov/199/Animal-Management-Unit). Arvada Animal Management Officers are highly trained and experienced professionals, certified through the Colorado Association of Animal Control Officers.

## Yard Disputes/Blowing Leaves into Street

Please do not rake or blow leaves and grass into the street. It is against [municipal code Sec. 94-6](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIICOOR_CH94STSICEOTPUPL_ARTIINGE_DIV1GE_S94-6DEETRUET) to do so.

## Parking Problems/Vehicles

All vehicles and trailers on public or private property must be operable and currently registered or stored out of public sight like in an enclosed garage. All vehicles and trailers must be parked on an approved surface (concrete, asphalt, or rock).

- **Recreational vehicles**, including trailers, can only be parked on the street for 72 hours in any given 7-day period. Recreational vehicles cannot be used for overnight accommodations (on private or public property).
- **Oversized vehicles** are **not**allowed on city streets. The City considers oversized vehicles to be anything longer than 25 feet in length or wider than 8 feet, a truck tractor or semi-trailer regardless of size (does not include RVs).

## Signs

Signs cannot be posted on any city right-of-way. This includes street signs, utility poles, and medians. Additionally, Realty signs are limited solely to the property that is "For Sale" or "For Rent." [View additional sign restrictions](https://www.arvadaco.gov/934/Sign-Placement). Please contact Planning at 720-898-7435 for sign permits information.

## Weeds

Weeds and non-decorative grasses over 12 inches high are prohibited. Noxious weeds are prohibited. It is the owner/occupant's responsibility to maintain the property out to the traveled portion of the roadway (including sidewalks, curbs, and gutters).

## Rubbish / Trash / Trash Containers

All property must be free from the accumulation of rubbish or garbage. This includes but is not limited to trash, tree branches, yard trimmings, metals, lumber, vehicle parts, appliances, etc. All trash must be removed from the property regularly so it won't become a nuisance. Trash containers **must**be stored behind the front face of the house, with the exception of your scheduled trash pickup day.

## Fences

**All**new fences or replacement fences require a permit. Please contact Planning at 720-898-7435 regarding permit requirements.

## Parking & Parking Surfaces

Off-street parking spaces and driveways must be made of asphalt or concrete. Additional parking surfaces may include rock as long as the area is clearly delineated and is kept free of weeds and visible dirt.

## Trees & Shrubs

Bushes/shrubbery growing over the sidewalks must be cut back to be even with the edge of the sidewalk. Tree branches hanging over the sidewalk must also be cut back to 10 feet above the sidewalk and 14' above the street. Plant growth cannot obstruct city signs or warning lights.
